clue.text: Messy cuff — that's annoying!

parts.note: to cuff someone is to slap them
'Dash!' is a mild exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone cuffed in a scuffle exclaims at the irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, so the result is messy.

clue.text: See 17
Noises off: a legal excuse for not appearing in court

definitions.text: a legal excuse for not appearing in court

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stage-direction 'noises off' set beside an archaic courtroom term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noises off' looks like a theatre direction, but 'off' signals rearranging NOISES.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic legal term for a formal excuse offered for a party's absence from court.

clue.text: Entertainment's over: attack 15

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: fun is entertainment; with the 's it gives funs
a fit is a sudden attack of illness

explanation.surface: The show has ended, and someone is struck down.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 points to the entry DIE; 'over' reverses the plural of fun, and 'Entertainment's over' reads like the end of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang idiom for dying, from snuffing out a candle.

clue.text: Celebrity bass, armed in the main?

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
the bass is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: A famous bass singer goes armed on the high seas?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic name for the sea, and this creature has arms, usually five.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea creature with radiating arms, so a cryptic description of an armed thing in the ocean.

clue.text: Acrobat's lacy tunic is lacking a bust

indicators.note: lacking says one letter, the a, is missing from the pool of letters
something bust is broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer's lacy costume lacks a bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of LACYTUNICIS and rearrange the rest; 'bust' looks anatomical but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider of a one-wheeled cycle is a circus performer, a kind of acrobat.

clue.text: 15 caught reversing without parking

indicators.note: without says a letter is left out
reversing tells us to read the word for caught backwards

parts.note: caught means trapped
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver was caught reversing outside a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns TRAPPED into DEPPART, and 'without' drops one P. 15 is DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart this life is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Heavily made-up singer J. Lo also changed name

indicators.note: changed means these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Jennifer Lopez, in heavy make-up, has also changed her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges JLOALSO into ALJOLSO, then N for name is added. The singer famously performed in blackface make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The American singer of The Jazz Singer, known for performing in heavy blackface make-up.

clue.text: Get bats outside in shade

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters go round the other word
bats here means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bring in bats from outside into the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals or cricket gear but means crazy, signalling the anagram of Get, which then sits outside 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight shade or tint of colour.

clue.text: See 26 down
Steer car with carbon deposit — that's beneath a university city!

parts.note: a steer is a bullock, an ox
a Ford is a make of car
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to lay something is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Someone steers a car and leaves a carbon deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: this geological layer lies under Oxford, the English university city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jurassic clay formation named after the rock underlying the area around Oxford.

clue.text: 15 numbers Charlie rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters read backwards

parts.note: a charlie is a fool, a sap

explanation.surface: Fifteen numbers are turned down by Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NOSSAP round as a whole; 15 is DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Stitching of suit ran out, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The stitching of a suit has sadly run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Suturation is the act of sewing, especially closing a wound with stitches.

clue.text: Elected Kitty to appear in 15 show

parts.note: a party elected is in

indicators.note: to appear in puts the kitty inside the other word

parts.note: 15 is the entry for a cube with spots
a kitty is a cat

explanation.surface: An elected cat appears in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a pot of money, but here it is a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point it out or show it.

clue.text: WC lacking sides and a spotted thing

indicators.note: and continues the list of what is lacking, adding the a
lacking sides removes the outermost letter at each end

parts.note: the ladies is a WC, a women's toilet

explanation.surface: A toilet without walls and a spotted object.
explanation.walkthrough: LADIES loses its sides L and S to give ADIE, 'and' the A goes too.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaming cube is marked with spots on each face.

clue.text: There's nothing better than half going east (see over)

indicators.note: the bracketed see over tells us to read the run backwards

parts.note: to see something is to spot it
HT is the abbreviation for half-time

explanation.surface: A note on a page: half heading east, turn over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see over' reads like 'turn the page'; reversed SPOT E HT gives the answer. 'going' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the best of all has nothing better than it.

clue.text: 15's dated advice to hard up Lancastrian dancer?

definitions.text: dated advice to hard up Lancastrian dancer?
definitions.meaning: old slang for pawning: a broke clog dancer from Lancashire should pawn their wooden shoes

explanation.surface: Advice for a Lancashire folk dancer who is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is dated slang for pawn; clog dancing is a Lancashire tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning to die, and literally to pawn wooden footwear.

clue.text: Old town house east of Morecambe, comically introduced by Jack

indicators.note: introduced by puts the jack first
east of means after, in an across clue

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian

explanation.surface: A house east of the seaside resort of Morecambe is comically introduced by Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the comedian Eric Morecambe of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is an ancient city whose walls fell in the Bible story.

clue.text: Hams broadcast with flat standard position

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Radio hams broadcast from a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hams' and 'broadcast' suggest radio, but 'broadcast' rearranges HAMS and FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and lowering it partway is a mourning position.

clue.text: Gaining Oscar, A-list celeb's top wobbled — not complaining!

indicators.note: gaining means taking in, so the O goes inside the rest
wobbled means shaken up, so the letters are rearranged
top means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An A-list star wins an Oscar and their composure wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbled' rearranges the A-list letters plus the C to give STICAL, and 'Gaining' puts the O in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoical person endures hardship without complaint.

clue.text: Chester's boundaries in river hollow over the hill

indicators.note: in places the boundary letters inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is the river that flows through Chester

indicators.note: boundaries means the outer letters of the word

parts.note: a pit is a hollow

explanation.surface: The edge of Chester lies on the river in a hollow, past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundaries' picks Chester's first and last letters; aptly, the Dee is the river that flows through Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone over the hill is past their prime, worn out by age.

clue.text: Bold, failing to start a symphony

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: bold means heroic

explanation.surface: A brave attempt fails at the start of a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' drops the H of HEROIC; A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony is called the Eroica.

clue.text: Removed, will they at last reveal if you have a lover?

definitions.text: Removed, will they at last reveal if you have a lover?

parts.words: Removed, will they at last reveal if you have a lover?
parts.note: the game of plucking parts of a flower one by one, saying loves me, loves me not, until the last decides

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether stripping something away will reveal a secret love.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulled one at a time from a daisy, these flower parts answer whether you are loved.

clue.text: Margaret briefly published 15

parts.note: Peg is a short form of the name Margaret
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: Margaret has had something briefly published.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is DIE; this is a slang phrase for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial idiom meaning to die.

clue.text: Really embarrassing coming to 15

definitions.meaning: in the old sense of mortify, putting to death, or flesh becoming dead tissue

explanation.surface: Dying would be truly embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is DIE; mortify once meant to kill, and mortification is the death of tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliating, and in the older sense, becoming dead or necrotic.

clue.text: See 5
Member said to make pictures the old way

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A member says pictures are made the old-fashioned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Limn is an archaic verb meaning to draw or paint.

clue.text: Flower birds almost sound like a Persian?

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a Persian cat makes a purring sound

explanation.surface: Birds almost sound like a Persian cat among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' is a breed of cat here, not a person from Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, a type of delphinium.

clue.text: See 17
Without question, Austria's lost expert on tank maintenance

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters go round
lost means astray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Austria has, without doubt, lost an expert at tank maintenance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question' reads as 'certainly'; 'Without' here means outside. 'lost' scrambles AUSTRIA to AUARIST, around Q.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarist keeps fish in aquarium tanks, a specialist in their care.
